Luffy.bio: Captain of the Straw Hat Pirates and Fifth Emperor of the Sea. His Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika awakening makes him the reincarnation of the Sun God — the most ridiculous and free Devil Fruit in the world.
Luffy.events: After toppling Kaido in Wano and the Nika reveal reshaped the world order, Luffy arrived at Elbaf accumulating allies. Emperor prestige and community hype at historic highs. Ch.1181: while eating to replenish strength, Luffy sensed Imu's Haki from across Elbaf and stopped cold — said he has never felt anything like it and immediately demanded more food. Imu's direct address of 'Isn't that right, Joy Boy' in the same chapter ties Luffy into the ancient conflict by name. Community reads the eating as Gear Fifth preparation. The final confrontation thesis strengthens with every chapter.

sbs.text: Birthday: May 5 — Children's Day in Japan. Oda chose it deliberately to reflect Luffy's childlike, unstoppable spirit of freedom.
Blood type: F. Luffy shares this blood type with Shanks and Gol D. Roger — one of the earliest quiet hints at their spiritual lineage connecting all three across generations.
On whether Luffy's mother is alive — Oda's answer: 'She's alive. I'll leave it at that for now. But she's not a gentle woman.' The fandom has been theorizing her identity ever since.

Zoro.bio: First mate of the Straw Hats and future World's Greatest Swordsman. He wields Enma, one of the 21 Great Grade swords, and has awakened Conqueror's Haki.
Zoro.events: His defeat of King in Wano confirmed his trajectory toward Mihawk. Enma mastery and Conqueror's Haki pushed stock sharply upward through Egghead. At Elbaf, a single strike from Imu neutralised him alongside the full Straw Hat crew — the first time Zoro has been rendered completely powerless without a fight. Community sentiment has sharply divided: bulls hold the Mihawk ceiling thesis, bears cite the Imu threat-level gap as a structural ceiling on his valuation.

sbs.text: Birthday: November 11 — 11/11. A date of repeating ones, fitting for a man defined by singular obsession. Some fans read it as three swords (1, 1) + one path (1) forward.
If the Straw Hats had real-world jobs — Zoro would be a police officer or security guard. Oda sees him as fundamentally a protector, not just a fighter.
Oda confirmed Zoro's name derives from François l'Ollonnais, a 17th-century French pirate. His ruthless reputation made him a fitting namesake for Oda's most relentless swordsman.

Nami.bio: Navigator of the Straw Hat Pirates and wielder of the Clima-Tact, capable of producing thunder clouds at will. Her mastery of weather manipulation continues to grow.
Nami.events: Steady stock reflecting stable community appreciation. No dramatic arc shifts post-Wano, but her importance as the crew's navigator keeps value firm.

sbs.text: Birthday: July 3. In Japanese, 'na' = 7, 'mi' = 3 — so 7/3 reads as 'Na-Mi.' One of Oda's earliest character birthday wordplay puns.
Real-world job: weatherwoman or meteorologist. Oda noted she already does this better than most professionals — the SBS just made it official.
Blood type: S (RH-). Oda revealed all Straw Hat blood types in SBS. Nami's rare blood type matches her rare navigational gift.

Usopp.bio: Sniper of the Straw Hats and self-proclaimed Brave Warrior of the Sea. Despite no Devil Fruit, his precision marksmanship and Pop Greens continue to prove pivotal.
Usopp.events: Steady valuation with slight growth post-Wano. Many fans speculate his God Usopp moment in the final arc will spike him dramatically when it arrives.

sbs.text: Birthday: April 1 — April Fools' Day. Oda chose this deliberately. Usopp is the crew liar, a self-proclaimed warrior who exaggerates everything — so his birthday is the world's most famous day for lies. Perfect.
Real-world job: Oda said Usopp would be a painter or illustrator. His Pop Green biology skills and inventive mind translate directly to artistic creation.

Oda acknowledged Usopp's design is inspired by Pinocchio — the lying boy whose nose grows. Usopp's long nose is a direct visual reference, with the same lie-and-grow mythology underlying his character arc.

Sanji.bio: Cook of the Straw Hats and third-strongest member. His Germa genetic enhancements activated in Wano, adding an exoskeleton and the devastating Ifrit Jambe technique.
Sanji.events: The Ifrit Jambe awakening in Wano nearly closed the Zoro gap, fueling fierce community debate. At Elbaf, Imu's one-shot incapacitated the entire crew simultaneously — Sanji included — without resistance. The event exposed a generational gap between the Straw Hats' current ceiling and the forces now in play. Stock remains volatile near the 2.5B range as the market prices in whether Elbaf is a temporary setback or a hard reset on his arc trajectory.

sbs.text: Birthday: March 2 — '3/2' in Japanese is 'san-ni,' which sounds like 'Sanji.' Classic Oda birthday wordplay. The same numbering trick used for most Straw Hat birthdays.

Sanji's swirled eyebrow curls in the opposite direction to Zoro's. Oda confirmed this is intentional — they are designed as mirror-image opposites in personality, philosophy, and even physical detail.
Real-world job: chef, obviously. But Oda specified he'd work in a French restaurant — fitting for a man who learned from a pirate cook and names his attacks in French.

Chopper.bio: Doctor of the Straw Hats who ate the Hito Hito no Mi, granting him a human mind and several transformation points. His Monster Point rivals mid-tier commanders.
Chopper.events: No dramatic power jumps since Wano. Chopper's value reflects consistent medical utility and beloved mascot status rather than combat speculation.

sbs.text: Birthday: December 24 — Christmas Eve. Oda chose it because Chopper is a reindeer. It is exactly as straightforward and charming as it sounds.
Oda confirmed Chopper can access far more than seven transformations with the Rumble Ball — those are simply the ones he has learned to control. His true potential remains unexplored.
Real-world job: a doctor, naturally. Oda added that Chopper would probably specialize in unusual or rare diseases — reflecting his outsider background and drive to cure the incurable.

Robin.bio: Archaeologist of the Straw Hats and the only person alive who can read the Poneglyphs. Her Hana Hana no Mi awakening lets her bloom body parts on any surface at scale.
Robin.events: Robin's Elbaf arc is the series' most significant single information acquisition event outside the Void Century itself. The reunion with Jaguar D. Saul — 22 years after Ohara, Robin having changed her hair to match how it looked as a child — was the emotional catalyst. The strategic revelation was the Owl Library: every book saved from Ohara's destruction, preserved in Elbaf, gigantified and intact. The World Government spent twenty years believing it had won. It hadn't. Robin's existing thesis — irreplaceable to the Void Century resolution — is now not speculation but confirmed infrastructure. The community's treatment of her as a floor-stable, high-certainty narrative hold has been validated. Her chart no longer moves on hope; it moves on proximity to answers. With Saul's library in reach and Imu's secrets beginning to surface, her valuation is structurally insulated from the downside volatility that affects more speculative positions.

sbs.text: Birthday: February 6. Oda chose it for Robin's elegance and reserved coolness — no wordplay, just a date that felt right for one of the series' most composed characters.
Real-world job: archaeologist. The only Straw Hat whose SBS dream job perfectly matches what she already does. Oda noted she would work in a museum or on excavation sites.
Blood type: S. Her rarity as the sole survivor of Ohara extends even into her blood type — shared with Nami, but Robin's carries the weight of a people erased from history.

Franky.bio: Shipwright of the Straw Hats and cyborg who rebuilt himself after a near-fatal accident. He crafted the Thousand Sunny and fights with a cola-powered body.
Franky.events: Vegapunk technology interactions in Egghead gave him a small bump. Fans expect a major role if the Sunny needs upgrades in the final saga.

sbs.text: Birthday: March 9 — '3/9' in Japanese is 'san-kyu,' which sounds like 'thank you' (arigato → sankyu). Franky's birthday is literally Thank You Day in Japan. Perfectly on-brand for a man who builds things as gifts.
Real-world job: carpenter or shipwright. Oda did not stray far — Franky's real-world self would still be building things, just without the cola-powered arms.

Oda confirmed Franky's pre-cyborg name 'Cutty Flam' was deliberately obscure — it references Scottish and Irish slang terms Oda found while researching pirate history. Tom's influence on naming conventions extended even here.

Brook.bio: Musician of the Straw Hats and undead skeleton who ate the Yomi Yomi no Mi. His Soul Solid sword and soul-manipulation powers make him an unpredictable fighter.
Brook.events: Consistent value through most of the series. In the Elbaf Arc, an on-panel memory sequence showed Brook and Holy Knight Manmayer Gunko holding hands — with Gunko reacting to the vision with 'FATHER!!' The nature of their connection remains unresolved, but the panel is canon and community speculation around Brook's past is now at an all-time high.

sbs.text: Birthday: April 3. In Japanese, 'yo-mi' can be read from 4 and 3 — and the Yomi Yomi no Mi is the underworld fruit. Oda confirmed this link: Brook's birthday literally spells out his Devil Fruit's name.
Real-world job: musician, naturally. Oda specified Brook would play in jazz clubs — a man 50 years out of time would fit perfectly into the timeless world of jazz.

Oda was asked how Brook uses his powers without a body. His explanation: the Yomi Yomi no Mi doesn't animate the bones — it creates a soul-shell that inhabits them. Brook's body is essentially haunted by himself.

Jinbe.bio: Helmsman of the Straw Hats and former Warlord of the Sea. A master of Fish-Man Karate, he can manipulate water itself as a weapon.
Jinbe.events: His official Straw Hat joining in Wano boosted stock meaningfully. Community values him as a stable floor pick — elite but not speculative.

Roger.bio: The King of the Pirates and only man to conquer the Grand Line. Roger had no Devil Fruit — he achieved everything through supreme mastery of Haki alone.
Roger.events: Gol D. Roger's stock operates on a different axis than any active character — pure historical valuation, and every final saga revelation compounds his legacy. The man who reached Laugh Tale, heard the True History, and chose to laugh rather than act represents the series' central thesis on inherited will. His execution speech — 'My treasure? If you want it, you can have it. Find it' — created the entire pirate era and all market activity that followed. The Void Century revelations throughout the final saga, the Joy Boy prophecy confirmation, and the Roger-Oden journals all retroactively elevate his positioning. Community treats him as the most premium historical hold in the market: no active plot risk, pure upside from every Final Saga revelation. The Roger thesis has never been wrong and shows no signs of reversing.

sbs.text: Blood type: XF. Oda confirmed Roger's blood type in SBS — shared with Zoro and Franky. XF is the rarest type. Oda never explained the significance directly, leaving the community to speculate about what Roger, Zoro, and Franky share beyond blood.

Across multiple SBS volumes Oda confirmed: Roger was not executed because the Marines could kill him. He was already dying of an incurable illness. He chose the time and place of his death — turning the World Government's execution into the greatest act of pirate defiance in history and sparking the Great Age of Piracy.

Oda confirmed in SBS that 'Gol D.' is Roger's true name — 'Gold Roger' was the World Government's deliberate mistranslation and suppression of his D. initial. The same pattern of erasing the Will of D. appears across the series.

Whitebeard.bio: The late 'Strongest Man in the World' and former Emperor. His Gura Gura no Mi could split the very air and create shockwaves powerful enough to sink islands.
Whitebeard.events: The 'Strongest Man in the World' designation made Whitebeard one of the market's most stable anchors for decades. His Marineford performance — holding off the entire Marine HQ while terminally ill, never turning his back — remains the benchmark against which community power evaluations are measured. Teach's betrayal and the theft of the Tremor Fruit represents the arc's most significant single wealth-transfer event. Post-death, his stock climbed steadily as Elbaf began surfacing his ties to the Giants and the God Valley Incident. The community treats him as a blue-chip historical hold: no active plot movement, but his role in the Void Century narrative keeps demand firm. Every Roger flashback and every God Valley reference compounds his premium retroactively.

sbs.text: Oda confirmed in SBS that Whitebeard genuinely never wanted treasure or the One Piece — he wanted family. His crew were his children in the truest sense. Oda said this was the character's core from the very beginning, never a late addition.

Birthday: April 6. No wordplay. Oda chose an early April date to place Whitebeard in spring — the season of beginnings. For a man whose death began the final era of One Piece, the seasonal irony is noted.

On whether Whitebeard was truly the world's strongest — Oda confirmed yes, at his prime. His injuries at Marineford (dozens of stab wounds, a missing half-jaw, having fought several Admirals simultaneously) mean his final stand was performed by a man already half-dead. That is the point.

Kaido.bio: Former Emperor of the Sea dubbed 'The Strongest Creature in the World.' His Azure Dragon Mythical Zoan and nigh-invincible body made him seemingly unkillable — until Wano.
Kaido.events: The strongest creature alive at his peak — an IPO that never dipped for forty years. Kaido's valuation was built on an unanswerable thesis: no one could kill him, and the market priced that in fully. Wano dismantled it in the most public way possible. Luffy's Gear Fifth breakthrough, the Elbaf Giant reinforcements, and the accumulated damage from the Nine Red Scabbards all contributed to the collapse. Sent to the Earth's core alongside Big Mom, his chart is a textbook peak-crash pattern. Community is split: bulls argue he'll return transformed by whatever force lies beneath Wano; bears treat him as a closed position. Historical floor remains extremely high — forty years of near-mythological dominance doesn't unwind overnight, and the Kaido thesis was never wrong about his raw ceiling.

Big Mom.bio: Former Emperor of the Sea and matriarch of the 85-child Charlotte Family. Her Soul-Soul Fruit takes lifespan to create Homies and imbue objects with souls.
Big Mom.events: Charlotte Linlin's valuation peaked during Whole Cake Island as the full scope of her Soru Soru no Mi — lifespan manipulation at a geopolitical scale — became clear. The Wano crash was definitive: sealed underground in Onigashima's magma chamber alongside Kaido, she exits active play entirely. Community debate mirrors her portfolio: bulls argue her Charlotte family empire continues operating independently, bears note that without her fear-based control the Big Mom Pirates are structurally compromised. Her floor is historically high — Yonko-class ceiling at peak is non-negotiable — but the chart clearly shows a closed arc. The soul-bound Homies, the Totto Land territory, and the family's sheer size keep her legacy valuation from collapsing entirely. Most analysts treat her as a legacy hold, not a speculative position.

Shanks.bio: Emperor of the Sea, Captain of the Red Hair Pirates, and the man who inspired Luffy to become a pirate. Possibly the most refined Conqueror's Haki user alive.
Shanks.events: The Elbaf arc delivered the most consequential single origin reveal in the site's history. Shanks is the son of Figarland Garling — Supreme Commander of the God Knights — making him a half-Celestial Dragon by birth, separated from the Figarland family during the God Valley Incident. His twin brother Shamrock leads the Holy Knights and considers Shanks a traitor for choosing pirate life over Marie Geoise. What once looked like mysterious outsider influence now reads as a deliberate defection from the world's highest institutional tier. Shanks holds leverage against the World Government from both inside and outside its power structure simultaneously — he knows every angle because he was born into it. His market premium has never been higher: the community was pricing in mystery, and the mystery resolved into something even more loaded than it speculated. The Luffy confrontation remains the most anticipated unpriced event on the site.

sbs.text: Birthday: March 9 — same as Mihawk and Franky. Three major characters sharing a birthday is not an accident. Shanks and Mihawk share a date as the two greatest swordsman rivals of their generation.
Blood type: F. Shared with Luffy and Roger — the three men most spiritually connected across generations. Whether intentional foreshadowing or not, Oda confirmed it without comment.

On losing his arm — Oda confirmed that Shanks absolutely could have used Haki to block the Sea King. He chose not to. The sacrifice was deliberate: Shanks gave his arm to show Luffy what it means to protect something you love. The Sea King was never the point.

Blackbeard.bio: Emperor of the Sea and the only known person to wield two Devil Fruits simultaneously. He holds both the Yami Yami no Mi (Darkness) and the Gura Gura no Mi (Quake).
Blackbeard.events: The Elbaf arc's God Valley flashback transformed Blackbeard from the final saga's most calculating accumulator into its most personally motivated one. Rocks D. Xebec — born Davy D. Xebec, descended from Davy D. Jones — is his father. Blackbeard carries direct D. lineage from the man Garp and Roger had to ally to stop. More critically: Imu used Domi Reversi at God Valley to transform Rocks into a mindless demon mid-rescue, then had every Davy Clan member killed — Blackbeard's family, his entire people, erased in one staged operation. He survived as an infant. The community's read on Blackbeard has been fundamentally repriced: what looked like naked ambition now reads as the longest-running revenge arc in the series. His positioning as the final saga's highest-upside speculative hold is unchanged, but the thesis beneath it has shifted from 'ambitious accumulator' to 'sole surviving heir of a genocided bloodline with a direct score to settle with Imu.'

Buggy.bio: Former Roger Pirate member, Emperor of the Sea, and Cross Guild co-founder. His Bara Bara no Mi makes him immune to cuts. A man eternally elevated beyond his actual power.
Buggy.events: Somehow achieved Emperor status despite limited combat ability. Cross Guild's bounty scheme made Mihawk and Crocodile effectively work for him, causing a massive stock surge.

Mihawk.bio: Mihawk is a member of the Cross Guild. Their role in the One Piece world shapes the power balance of the seas.
Mihawk.events: Stock reflects Mihawk's ongoing role in the world. Community valuation is based on faction strength, recent arc relevance, and speculation on future story impact. Ch.1181: Imu deployed a sword technique in the Loki fight nearly identical to Mihawk's signature slash at Luffy in Marineford — same arc, same scale, same hawk eyes. The community upscale is immediate: if the world's true ruler fights like Mihawk, the 'Fraudhawk' slander takes a direct hit. Sword lineage theorists are running.

Crocodile.bio: Former Warlord and Cross Guild co-founder. His Sand-Sand Fruit can dehydrate anything to dust. Escaped Impel Down with Luffy and fought at Marineford.
Crocodile.events: Cross Guild's founding sparked a community re-evaluation. His stock climbed sharply when revealed as the key power behind Buggy's unlikely Emperor title.

sbs.text: A fan asked if Ivankov knew Crocodile from 'when he was a woman.' Oda's response: 'Ufufufu... I wonder? There are things in this world you just can't ask about. Ufufufu. I'm sure a real man like you would understand.' The community consensus: Oda confirmed it. Ivankov's leverage over Crocodile was knowledge of his past.

Oda confirmed Crocodile's hook is his own design choice — he had it installed after losing his hand in a past battle. The weapon hidden in it (poison or blade) was intentionally left vague to keep his history mysterious.
Birthday: September 5. No confirmed wordplay, but the community has noted that 9/5 — 'ku-go' — can mean 'suffering' in Japanese. A fitting date for a man defined by bitterness and defeat.

Daz Bonez.bio: Daz Bonez is a member of the Cross Guild. Their role in the One Piece world shapes the power balance of the seas.
Daz Bonez.events: Stock reflects Daz Bonez's ongoing role in the world. Community valuation is based on faction strength, recent arc relevance, and speculation on future story impact.

Hancock.bio: Empress of Amazon Lily and the 'Pirate Empress.' Her Mero Mero no Mi turns anyone who feels love or lust for her to stone — making her nearly untouchable.
Hancock.events: Amazon Lily's conflict with Blackbeard's crew spiked drama. Her protection of Luffy's allies and subsequent community recognition pushed her stock noticeably upward.

sbs.text: Oda confirmed Hancock is the most beautiful woman in the One Piece world — not just in reputation, but as a narrative fact. Her beauty is treated as a literal superpower: it clouds judgement, breaks rules, and bypasses logic.

On how the Mero Mero no Mi works — Oda clarified that it requires the target to feel genuine attraction. Pure-hearted or sufficiently distracted individuals are immune. This explains why Luffy is her greatest weakness: he genuinely doesn't see her that way.

Birthday: September 2. Oda chose it to align with the Kuja arc release window. No specific wordplay, but the date lands in the same month as Marine Ford's events — Hancock's most important arc began and ended in September's release schedule.

Law.bio: Captain of the Heart Pirates and Surgeon of Death. His Ope Ope no Mi creates a Room where he can freely swap, teleport, and dissect anything — including Conqueror's users.
Law.events: Law's defeat of Doflamingo and near-death at Big Mom's hands in Wano shaped his chart. Post-Wano stock settled at a respected tier reflecting earned battle credentials.

sbs.text: Law's full name was confirmed as 'Trafalgar D. Water Law' — the hidden middle initial D. shocked the community. Law carries the Will of D, placing him among the most significant people in the world's hidden history. Oda revealed this quietly, letting the weight land without fanfare.

Law's hometown of Flevance, the 'White City,' was named for its amber lead mineral — a slow poison the World Government concealed from its people. Oda drew maps and population charts in SBS to show the scope of the cover-up. The entire city was systematically wiped out.

Birthday: October 6 — '10/6' in Japanese doesn't have an obvious wordplay reading, but Oda placed it at a point when Law was being established as a key rival-ally to Luffy. Community has long noted that 10/6 = Tora-fa (tiger), fitting his tiger-themed tattoos.

Moria.bio: Former Warlord and 'Corpse King' of Thriller Bark. His Shadow-Shadow Fruit lets him steal shadows to create zombie armies or power himself up to terrifying scale.
Moria.events: His survival after near-death at Doflamingo's hands and reported Cross Guild ties is a welcome surprise. Stock holds with mild upward bias on potential return.

Doflamingo.bio: Former King of Dressrosa and Warlord. His String-String Fruit Awakening could weave threads capable of slicing cities. A Celestial Dragon by birth who renounced his lineage.
Doflamingo.events: Imprisoned in Impel Down since Dressrosa. Stock in steady decline since his defeat. His knowledge of Celestial Dragon secrets keeps community interest from fading entirely.

Bellamy.bio: Spring Hopper Bellamy, a former Donquixote Pirate with a grudging respect for Luffy. His Spring-Spring Fruit compresses his legs into devastating bouncing attacks.
Bellamy.events: His Dressrosa arc redemption — choosing not to kill Luffy even under direct orders — was a touching close to his journey. Stock flat post-closure.

Ace.bio: Son of Gol D. Roger and Luffy's sworn brother. His Mera Mera no Mi made him a Whitebeard Division Commander — until his execution at Marineford changed the world.
Ace.events: Ace's death at Marineford remains the series' defining tragedy. His stock peaked at that moment and holds as an eternal legend flat — an untouchable historical number.

sbs.text: Birthday: January 1 — New Year's Day. Ace is born on the first day of the year, the son of the Pirate King. Oda chose it so that Ace's existence would feel like the beginning of a new era — which, in every sense, it was.

Oda confirmed that Ace's father being Roger was intentionally hidden from readers for years. The reveal was one of the most carefully managed secrets in manga history — most of the editorial staff did not know either.

Blood type: S. Ace shares this blood type with several key figures. Oda confirmed in SBS that Ace's blood type was chosen to contrast with Luffy's F-type — they are brothers, but their blood is different. Their bond is chosen, not inherited.

Kidd.bio: Captain of the Kidd Pirates with a Magnet-Magnet Fruit letting him manipulate metal. His aggression and rivalry with Luffy drove him to the top of the Supernova generation.
Kidd.events: Defeated Big Mom in Wano alongside Law — a landmark moment. His subsequent crushing defeat by Shanks and reported limb loss tanked his stock post-Elbaf significantly.

Killer.bio: First mate of the Kidd Pirates known for scythe-bladed arm weapons. A non-Devil Fruit user who competes through blade speed and unpredictable attack angles.
Killer.events: His redemption from SMILE drug torture and defeat of Hawkins was a fan-favorite Wano moment. Stock noticeably pushed upward by the emotional resonance.

Apoo.bio: Captain of the On-Air Pirates with the Oto Oto no Mi (Sound) — his music is a literal weapon causing explosions and cuts to anyone who hears it.
Apoo.events: Played informant in Wano. His erratic allegiances keep stock perpetually volatile with no clear sustained trend in either direction.

Hawkins.bio: Captain of the Hawkins Pirates with the Wara Wara no Mi (Straw). He can redirect damage received to straw effigies linked to others, making himself nearly impossible to kill.
Hawkins.events: Switched allegiance to Kaido in Wano, then lost to Killer. Stock dipped following his defeat and subsequent absence from major story developments.

Bege.bio: Captain of the Fire Tank Pirates with the Castle-Castle Fruit — his body is a literal fortress housing soldiers and cannons. Nearly took Big Mom's head in Whole Cake Island.
Bege.events: His major role in the Whole Cake Island assassination plot set a high baseline. Stock holds at respectable mid-tier pirate captain level.

Urouge.bio: Captain of the Fallen Monk Pirates from Birka Sky Island. His unnamed fruit converts damage received into raw strength — absorbing punishment to hit back harder.
Urouge.events: Largely off-screen in major arcs. Stock flat with modest rise on mystery premium. Community awaits his return with growing curiosity.

Bonney.bio: Captain of the Bonney Pirates and Vegapunk's surrogate daughter. Her Toshi Toshi no Mi controls age — of others and herself. Her father Kuma's story broke the community's heart.
Bonney.events: Her Egghead role — revealing Kuma's past and briefly accessing the Nika transformation — caused a massive stock surge. One of Egghead's most important characters.

King.bio: All-Star of the Beast Pirates and last known survivor of the Lunarian race — a god-like tribe that can survive in any environment and generate fire from their bodies.
King.events: His defeat at Zoro's hands and the Lunarian revelation made his arc one of Wano's best. Stock peaked then declined with his capture and the race's secret exposed.

Queen.bio: All-Star of the Beast Pirates with the Spinosaurus Ancient Zoan and a brilliant scientific mind. Created the Ice Oni virus and numerous cyborg weapons.
Queen.events: His Sanji fight showcased scientific creativity and sharp comedy. Defeated and imprisoned, his stock peaked in Wano and declined consistently post-arc.

Jack.bio: All-Star of the Beast Pirates with a 1 billion beri bounty. His Mammoth Ancient Zoan and relentless brutality destroyed the elephant Zou's body surface in mere hours.
Jack.events: Jack's multiple defeats in Wano contributed to the Beast Pirates' collapse. Stock remains at beast-tier captain level but without upward momentum.

Ulti.events: Stock reflects Ulti's ongoing role in the world. Community valuation is based on faction strength, recent arc relevance, and speculation on future story impact.

Who's Who.bio: A former CP9 agent who was imprisoned in Impel Down after losing the Gomu Gomu no Mi to Shanks — a fact so classified the World Government tried to erase the Nika legend itself. He escaped, ate the Neko Neko no Mi, Model: Saber Tiger, and clawed his way into Kaido's Tobi Roppo. The only Wano antagonist whose backstory directly intersects with the Nika mystery.
Who's Who.events: His defeat by Jinbe was lopsided, but the revelation that he knew about the Sun God Nika — knowledge supposedly wiped from history — is his primary lore value. Stock crashed on the defeat result; the Nika connection provides a floor that pure combat performance would not.

Katakuri.events: His narrow loss to Luffy in Whole Cake Island was the arc's emotional peak. That defeat caused a community dip, but his near-equal showing keeps the baseline extremely high.

Bartolomeo.bio: Bartolomeo is a member of the Barto Club. Their role in the One Piece world shapes the power balance of the seas.
Bartolomeo.events: The Elbaf arc delivered Bartolomeo's most revealing moment and his most expensive lesson. Punished by the Red Hair Pirates for burning Shanks' flag on their territory, he was presented with a test dressed as a threat: administer a poison to Luffy, or face consequences. His choice required no deliberation — he drank it himself. The poison was fake. Yasopp's subsequent sinking of the Going Luffy-senpai was the real punishment: measured, permanent, and without cruelty. The scene reframes Bartolomeo not as a comedy fanboy but as someone whose conviction is structurally load-bearing. His market position remains what it has always been — a leveraged bet on Luffy's ceiling — but the Elbaf arc confirmed that the lever is genuine. He'll sacrifice the ship, the flag, and himself. The community's floor estimate on Bartolomeo moved up meaningfully; his comedy premium is now underpinned by demonstrated resolve.

Garp.bio: The 'Hero of the Marines' and grandfather of Luffy. Never ate a Devil Fruit — earning his legendary status through pure Haki and physical power alone. Cornered Gold Roger twice.
Garp.events: The Hero of the Marines' final arc as an active combatant peaked at Hachinosu. His self-authorized rescue mission to recover Coby from Blackbeard's sovereign base — defying Marine command, going in with a skeleton crew — was the most in-character reckless thing Garp has ever done on-panel. The battle with Kuzan, his former protégé turned Blackbeard officer, was the most emotionally weighted fight of the post-Wano period. Garp's subsequent capture confirmed what the community had long suspected: his era of individual dominance is closing. But his stock climbs on the Monkey D. family portfolio thesis regardless — every Dragon chapter, every Luffy chapter, and every Roger flashback adds historical premium to the patriarch who bridges all three. He trades at a meaningful premium above his active combat valuation on family legacy alone.

sbs.text: Oda confirmed in SBS that Garp was offered the rank of Admiral multiple times and refused every time. His reason: becoming Admiral would place him directly under the Gorosei's authority. Garp serves the Marines — not the World Government. A distinction that costs him rank but preserves his freedom.
On Garp's famous dog-head Marine helmet — Oda confirmed it is part of his personal uniform, chosen by Garp himself. It has no tactical purpose. He just likes dogs.

Birthday: May 2. No confirmed wordplay. Oda said Garp's date was chosen for the early May holiday window in Japan — a time of energy and celebration. Fitting for a man who punches boulders for training.

Loki.bio: Prince of Elbaf and the 'Accursed Prince' — imprisoned in chains under accusation of killing his own father, King Harald. His Devil Fruit grants him a transformation tied to Nidhogg, the mythical Norse dragon-serpent that gnaws at the roots of the World Tree. In Norse mythology, Nidhogg is an eternal, pre-creation force of destruction — and when Imu reacted to his transformation with 'Nidhogg… thou really hast returned,' the implication was clear: this power predates the current age of the world.
Loki.events: The Elbaf reveal showed him imprisoned in chains — a prince unable to act. Early hype collapsed. Ch.1181 reversed that entirely: transformed into full Nidhogg form and unleashed Thorheim, his strongest technique. The context driving his resolve: Harald died at 144 years old — half a giant's natural lifespan of 300 — and Loki holds Imu directly responsible for manipulating and killing his father. The battle is ideological as much as physical: Loki categorically rejected Imu's Domination philosophy, framing the fight as freedom against control — an ancient struggle continuing through him. Imu's response confirmed the Nidhogg is something he recognises from before, calling out 'thou really hast returned.' This is not a prince who lost. The market is repricing what Loki actually is.

sbs.text: Loki's Devil Fruit has not been officially named yet. Based on his confirmed Nidhogg transformation in Ch.1181, the community's leading theory is a Mythical Zoan modelled after Nidhogg — the world-serpent of Norse mythology that endlessly gnaws at the roots of Yggdrasil, representing entropy and the force that opposes the gods. Oda's Elbaf arc draws heavily from Norse myth, and Loki's fruit name confirmation is among the arc's most anticipated reveals.

Dorry.bio: Co-captain of the Giant Warrior Pirates who dueled Brogy for 100 years on Little Garden over an argument neither could remember. A legend of Elbaf's warrior culture.
Dorry.events: Dorry's Elbaf arc chart traces the arc's full emotional range. The resolution of Domi Reversi — the century-long sword duel with Brogy ending at last — was the arc's first major valuation spike, a beloved twenty-five-year payoff that pushed both giants to their historic high. The demonization by the Holy Knights (transformed into loyal demons via the Power of Evil) was the market's sharpest single-arc reversal: Dorry turned from protector to weapon, used against the people he'd spent a century belonging to. Zoro and Chopper's restoration in chapter 1178 closes the bracket, but the arc permanently elevated his narrative weight from Little Garden nostalgia to Final Saga participant. His valuation returns to its post-duel baseline, but the community's understanding of what he represents — a giant who chose loyalty over a century of exile — has deepened considerably.

Brogy.bio: Co-captain of the Giant Warrior Pirates and Dorry's eternal dueling partner. Their century-long rivalry is a foundational legend of the One Piece world.
Brogy.events: Brogy's Elbaf arc mirrors Dorry's precisely — they have shared every chart movement for a hundred years and the Elbaf arc continues the pattern. The Domi Reversi resolution was the community celebration the site was built for: twenty-five years of anticipation paying off in a single chapter. The demonization arc was its dark counterpart — Brogy transformed into a weapon against Elbaf's people by the Holy Knights, before Zoro and Chopper restored him in chapter 1178. His valuation returns to the post-resolution baseline, meaningfully above the pre-Elbaf floor. The community has long treated Dorry and Brogy as a paired position — buying one without the other is considered an asymmetric bet against their entire narrative logic. Their charts have never meaningfully diverged and show no signs of doing so. Whatever the final saga brings for one, it brings for both.

Dragon.bio: Supreme Commander of the Revolutionary Army and the world's most wanted criminal. Father of Luffy. His powers remain completely unconfirmed, fueling endless high-value speculation.
Dragon.events: Monkey D. Dragon remains the market's greatest information asymmetry — a character whose Devil Fruit, power ceiling, and true motivations have never been confirmed on-panel. The Revolutionary Army's Levely operation (liberating Kuma, directly assaulting Celestial Dragons inside Marie Geoise) was the first concrete proof that Dragon operates at the highest political tier. Sabo's survival and his eyewitness account of Imu's existence created a direct line between Dragon's intelligence network and the final saga's core conspiracy. Community consensus: Dragon knows more about the Void Century and Imu than any living character outside the World Government. His stock climbs on every Revolutionary Army chapter and peaks whenever Imu's power is displayed — the implied confrontation is the most anticipated political match in the series.

sbs.text: Oda was asked about the large tattoo on Dragon's face — a red pattern running from his left eye. His response: he drew it initially because 'it looks cool,' but later acknowledged it carries the feeling of a warrior's marking — someone who has been through something that left a permanent mark. He left the meaning open deliberately.

Birthday: October 5. No wordplay confirmed. Oda noted Dragon's birthday falls in autumn — a season of revolution and change. Whether intentional or not, October is historically the month of several real-world revolutions.

Multiple SBS questions asked what Dragon's Devil Fruit is. Oda has refused to answer every single time. This sustained silence across dozens of volumes is itself a statement — Dragon's power is being held for a specific narrative moment.

Enel.events: Currently on the moon doing robot archaeology. Community meme gold. Stock stable with nostalgia and final-saga return speculation keeping the floor firm and rising.

Imu.bio: The true ruler of the world, sitting atop the Empty Throne in Mariejois. Imu's age, identity, and powers remain largely mysterious — their fruit appears to be a monstrous dark entity capable of erasing nations. In ch.1180, Imu demonstrated a technique called Omen — an ability that takes radically different forms depending on the target. In ch.1181, Imu confirmed their abilities fall under the name 'Dominion,' and deployed a sword technique visually near-identical to Mihawk's signature slash at Luffy during Marineford — same arc, same scale, same hawk-like eyes. Imu also carries a personal flashback involving a silhouetted figure confirmed as Joy Boy, and screamed 'Isn't that right, Joy Boy' while releasing a massive Haki burst — the first direct confirmation that Imu and Joy Boy have a personal, ancient history.
Imu.events: The Egghead Incident confirmed Imu's personal involvement in erasing Lulusia Kingdom. Arrived at Elbaf and freed the Holy Knights, then one-shotted Zoro and Sanji simultaneously using Omen — no fight, no resistance. Ch.1181: engaged Loki directly and named the three pillars of Domination for the first time: Corruption (power too easily gained), Covenants (servitude chosen out of self-interest), and Omen (envy of those who seek their goal). Wields a sword named Nemesis. The Joy Boy revelation landed in the same chapter — Imu's relationship with Joy Boy was not hostile but described as 'quite friendly,' raising deep questions about how that alliance collapsed into the Void Century conflict. Responded to Loki's Nidhogg Thorheim with a smile and the words 'thou really hast returned.' Community stock at all-time high with no visible ceiling.

Saturn.bio: One of the Five Elders with authority over Science and Defense. He transformed into a monstrous spider-like demon during the Egghead siege — and was killed by Luffy.
Saturn.events: Jaygarcia Saturn's arc follows the most dramatic peak-crash pattern on the site. At Egghead's opening he represented the most terrifying institutional force in the One Piece world: a Five Elder with a mythical Gyuki transformation, immunity to conventional attacks, and personal oversight of Vegapunk's Devil Fruit and Void Century research. The Egghead siege progressively dismantled his invincibility thesis — Bonney's Distorted Future aging him into vulnerability, Nika's direct confrontation stripping his regeneration, and ultimately his death at the arc's conclusion. His chart is a textbook information-risk case study: the community bought his mystery premium at full price and sold his resolution at near-zero. The lesson his chart teaches is that institutional secrecy is a depreciating asset once the narrative decides to resolve it.

Mars.bio: One of the Five Elders with authority over Environment. Transforms into an enormous bird-like demon form. A key enforcer of the World Government's most extreme orders.
Mars.events: Mars represents the Five Elders' information-warfare function — his Itsumade mythical bird Zoan and his role coordinating the Egghead communications blackout make him the most institutionally significant Elder for the final saga's media war. His defining arc moment was the attempted suppression of Vegapunk's death message: deploying across the Grand Line to intercept a broadcast that ultimately reached the world anyway. That failure is the community's most bullish signal for the information-freedom thesis — Morgans, Robin, and the broader network of truth-seekers represent direct hedges against Mars's influence. His chart climbs steadily as the Final Saga's Void Century information war becomes the dominant narrative thread. Whoever ultimately defeats Mars defeats the World Government's most powerful censorship mechanism.

Warcury.bio: One of the Five Elders with authority over Military Affairs. His demon form is boar-like with overwhelming brute force. Among the Gorosei's most aggressive front-line fighters.
Warcury.events: Warcury's Egghead performance established him as the Five Elders' blunt-force instrument — his Fushi mythical Zoan transformation displayed raw physical power at a tier that overwhelmed conventional opposition. Unlike Saturn (institutional oversight) or Mars (information control), Warcury reads as a pure combat position: limited confirmed plot significance, but an exceptionally high ceiling on that combat. Community treats him as a low-information, high-ceiling hold — the type of character whose valuation can spike dramatically the moment a matchup is confirmed. His chart shows steady accumulation from power-scaling analysts while narrative-focused investors remain cautious. The bullish thesis is simple: a Five Elder whose only demonstrated function is destruction will eventually be pointed at someone the community deeply cares about.

Nusjuro.bio: Nusjuro is a member of the Gorosei / World Government. Their role in the One Piece world shapes the power balance of the seas.
Nusjuro.events: Among the surviving Five Elders, Nusjuro carries the highest speculative premium from the swordsmanship community. His Bakotsu mythical Zoan transformation and his single-arc elimination of Vegapunk's entire Pacifista fleet demonstrated operational efficiency that shocked the community's power-scaling analysts. Post-Egghead, his continued Final Saga presence keeps his chart in steady accumulation. The implied Mihawk comparison — both operating as the world's premier swordsmen in their respective institutional roles — has created substantial speculative demand that may not resolve until a direct on-panel confrontation forces a verdict. Community consensus: Nusjuro is a high-conviction long position for investors who believe the swordsmanship arc of the final saga has significant chapters remaining.

Ju Peter.bio: Ju Peter is a member of the Gorosei / World Government. Their role in the One Piece world shapes the power balance of the seas.
Ju Peter.events: Ju Peter's Sandworm mythical Zoan — a creature that consumes at geological scale — was the most visually dominant Five Elder reveal during the Egghead siege. His positioning mirrors Warcury's: high physical ceiling, limited confirmed narrative role, steady accumulation from power-scaling investors. The Five Elders collectively represent the most durable antagonist tier in the final saga — individually beatable in specific contexts, never fully confronted as a group. Ju Peter's specific chart catalyst will be whoever his eventual opponent is confirmed to be. Community speculation has rotated through Zoro, Law, and Sabo as candidate matchups, each rotation producing a minor valuation spike in those characters. Until confirmation, he trades as a pure mystery premium — a position the community is comfortable holding given the Five Elders' proven narrative longevity.

Shamrock.bio: Shamrock is a member of the Gorosei / World Government. Their role in the One Piece world shapes the power balance of the seas.
Shamrock.events: Figarland Shamrock arrived in Elbaf as the Holy Knights' Commander and the arc's most structurally interesting antagonist. As Shanks' older twin brother and Garling's son, he is everything Shanks chose not to be: fully committed to the World Government, contemptuous of the lower world, and executing an annexation agenda that treats Elbaf's literacy and independence as obstacles to remove. His ultimatum — destroy the school and the Owl Library or the children die — encapsulates the World Government's institutional logic perfectly. Community treats Shamrock as a high-conviction short-term antagonist with limited standalone narrative runway: his arc resolves when the Figarland family confrontation resolves, and his chart is deeply correlated with Shanks'. The Shamrock position is structurally a proxy bet on when and how the twin brother confrontation concludes. He's priced as a lever, not a destination.

Shepherd Sommers.bio: A Holy Knight of the World Government — elite warriors serving directly under Imu, revealed dramatically during the Elbaf Arc. Little is known of their individual powers.
Shepherd Sommers.events: Shepherd Sommers delivered the Elbaf arc's most institutionally precise moment: the ultimatum. Destroy both the Walrus School and the Owl Library, or ten children die. No combat display, no power reveal — just the World Government's leverage system applied with surgical efficiency against people who had no answer to it. Sommers represents the God Knights' administrative function: the voice that translates Imu's institutional will into terms communities cannot refuse. His market position reflects that role cleanly. Community treats him as a high-certainty mid-tier antagonist with a clearly defined ceiling — built to make the road to the endgame costly, not to be the endgame himself. His valuation holds firm at the God Knight institutional floor: meaningful enough to hold as a final saga position, not speculative enough to chase for upside.

Rimoshifu Killingham.bio: A Holy Knight of the World Government — one of Imu's direct enforcers. Debuted in the Elbaf Arc alongside the other Holy Knights, immediately drawing comparisons to the Admirals.
Rimoshifu Killingham.events: Where Sommers issued the ultimatum, Killingham enforced compliance. When the Giants hesitated to burn their own school, Killingham compelled the giant Ange to set the fire — the Elbaf arc's most emotionally targeted act of institutional violence, and Killingham's fingerprints are directly on it. He represents the God Knights' operational enforcement arm: less diplomatic than Sommers, more direct than Gunko, with no unresolved mystery premium attached to his positioning. Community reads him exactly as he presents — a reliable mid-tier antagonist whose role is to make sure the orders get carried out regardless of hesitation. His chart holds steady alongside Sommers as the God Knights' functional enforcement pair, clearly distinct from Gunko's speculative tier above them.

Manmayer Gunko.bio: A Holy Knight of the World Government and one of the few female members of the elite order. Her combat style and abilities remain to be fully explored in the Elbaf Arc.
Manmayer Gunko.events: The most strategically loaded God Knight in the site's current portfolio. Three overlapping theses drive her premium above the other Elbaf God Knights. First: she was the vessel Imu chose for direct possession in chapter 1178 — not coincidence but selection, implying a pre-existing connection between Gunko and Imu that the community is actively pricing. Second: a Flower Room silhouette matching her outline appears alongside Imu in a flashback — unconfirmed, but the community treats it as speculative premium rather than noise. Third: the Brook thesis. A flashback shows a young Gunko holding hands with Brook before he ever sailed as a pirate, and she is a documented fan of his Soul King recordings. The 'Brook's daughter' theory has not been confirmed or denied — and in this market, sustained ambiguity on a thesis this emotionally charged is pure speculative fuel. Her chart carries all three premiums simultaneously and they compound rather than cancel. The Imu possession alone justifies a tier above the other God Knights. The Brook connection makes her one of the most unique asymmetric positions on the site.

Rocks.bio: The most dangerous man in history before Roger. Captain of the legendary Rocks Pirates, whose crew included Whitebeard, Big Mom, and Kaido. He sought to become King of the World.
Rocks.events: The Elbaf arc's God Valley flashback delivered the complete reframe. Rocks D. Xebec — born Davy D. Xebec on God Valley itself, descendant of Davy D. Jones, the 'previous king of the world' — did not attack God Valley for conquest. He came to rescue his wife and infant son (Marshall D. Teach) from the Celestial Dragon hunting competition. Imu deployed Domi Reversi mid-battle to transform him into a mindless demon, forcing Roger and Garp's alliance to stop his own body — and ensuring history would record him as a monster rather than a father. The God Valley Incident was staged to kill him. The community's treatment of Rocks as a pure power-speculation hold is now obsolete: he's a tragedy, and every Blackbeard chapter retroactively revalues his chart. The question his arc poses — whether Blackbeard will complete what his father was killed for — is now the final saga's most structurally loaded open position.

Harald.events: His debut as King of Elbaf drove the strongest Giant-faction stock surge since Little Garden speculation. Ch.1181 recontextualised him entirely: Harald died at 144 years old — giants live to approximately 300 — meaning he died at roughly half his natural lifespan. Loki believes Imu manipulated and ultimately killed his father, and Harald's sacrifice is the emotional core driving Loki's confrontation with Imu. His death now reads as a World Government-engineered removal of a Giant king who represented a genuine threat. Stock reflects legacy value — Harald's role in the arc grows the more Loki's story unfolds.

Joy Boy.bio: A figure from 800 years ago who left an apology on the Mermaid's Poneglyph and created the treasure One Piece. Directly connected to Luffy's awakening as Nika.
Joy Boy.events: Each Void Century revelation elevates Joy Boy's stock. The community's understanding of him as the original Nika drives maximum speculation value into every arc. Ch.1181: Imu had a direct personal flashback to a silhouetted image of himself and Joy Boy — and screamed 'Isn't that right, Joy Boy' while releasing a Haki burst powerful enough to reach Luffy across Elbaf. First confirmed on-panel evidence that Imu and Joy Boy have a direct, personal, ancient history. Whatever happened 800 years ago between them is the series' true center. Stock surges to near-Imu levels.

The Man Marked by Flames.bio: A mysterious figure teased at the end of Wano — referred to by Garp as a lurking legend. No confirmed details about appearance, identity, or power. Their existence alone has set the community on fire.
The Man Marked by Flames.events: First mentioned at Wano Peak, his stock has been on a pure hype climb ever since. Zero confirmed details equals maximum community speculation premium.

Garling.bio: Supreme Commander of the God's Knights and former King of God Valley. A swordsman of supreme caliber, widely believed to be Shanks' biological father.
Garling.events: The Elbaf arc confirmed Garling's position as the most consequential figure in One Piece's institutional power structure below Imu. Supreme Commander of the Holy Knights and father of both Shanks and Shamrock — his portfolio sits at the exact intersection of the World Government's enforcement arm and the series' most charged unresolved origin story. His twin sons represent the fork in the road between compliance and rebellion: one became the world's most celebrated pirate, the other its most loyal instrument of suppression. Both emerged from the same bloodline he produced with a red-haired woman outside Marie Geoise. The community's read on Garling has shifted from 'powerful antagonist' to 'structural nexus' — he doesn't need to be the strongest man in the room to determine the final saga's outcome. His chart climbs not on combat speculation but on proximity to Imu and on the Shanks-family confrontation thesis.

Rayleigh.bio: Rayleigh is a member of the Roger Pirates (retired). Their role in the One Piece world shapes the power balance of the seas.
Rayleigh.events: Silvers Rayleigh — the Dark King, Roger's first mate — occupies a unique market position: the most proven active fighter whose true ceiling is deliberately kept ambiguous by the narrative. His two-year Haki training of Luffy at Rusukaina established the foundational mechanics of advanced Haki, and every Gear Fifth chapter compounds his legacy as the man who built the final saga's protagonist. His Egghead appearance to delay Kizaru — buying the Straw Hats escape time by engaging an admiral — was the community's clearest on-panel signal that Rayleigh still operates near the top of the active-fighter market despite his age. Stock trades at a consistent premium above any comparable retired character: the Roger crew thesis, the unfinished business speculation, and his role as the final saga's most credible living witness to the True History all support steady long-term accumulation.

Scopper Gaban.bio: A member of the Roger Pirates alongside Rayleigh, and one of Roger's most trusted warriors. His reappearance in the current era confirms he survived the crew's disbanding and remains a force.
Scopper Gaban.events: Scopper Gaban's Elbaf reveal was one of the arc's quietest and most resonant moments. Living for over twenty years in Elbaf under the alias 'Ya-san,' the man Roger called his Left Hand had been watching, waiting, and teaching history — invisible to the World Government, known to the Giants. His confirmation as the Left Hand of the Pirate King immediately elevated his market position to the second tier of the Roger crew legacy holds, behind only Rayleigh. His presence during Harald's final moments — attempting to stop Harald alongside Shanks — and his designation of Shanks as the 'child of fate' establishes him as the arc's living institutional memory: the man who knew Roger best and has been quietly positioning for the final saga's resolution for two decades. Community has begun treating him as a Roger-proxy investment: canonically underweighted relative to his narrative significance, with substantial upside when the endgame confirms his role.

Bentham.bio: Mr. 2 Bon Clay of Baroque Works — an okama warrior with the Clone-Clone Fruit who can perfectly replicate any face and body. His sacrifice at Impel Down to save Luffy is one of the series' greatest friendship moments.
Bentham.events: Bon Clay's self-sacrifice at Impel Down — staying behind to ensure Luffy escaped — is one of the most beloved scenes in the series. He now rules as Newkama Warden, and community stock holds high on nostalgia and final saga return hope.

X Drake.bio: Red Flag X Drake — a Supernova with an Allosaurus Ancient Zoan, secretly operating as a Marine SWORD agent inside Kaido's crew. A former Rear Admiral turned pirate turned double-agent.
X Drake.events: His SWORD reveal mid-Wano was a shocking twist that pushed stock upward sharply. His post-Wano fate remains uncertain, keeping community speculation active and his chart volatile.

Koala.bio: Revolutionary Army officer and close ally of Sabo. The child Fisher Tiger once freed, Koala grew up in the Revolutionary Army and mastered Fishman Karate. A key figure in the Army's intelligence network.
Koala.events: Her Dressrosa and Reverie involvement alongside Sabo drove steady stock growth. As the Revolutionary Army moves into the final saga's center stage, community expects her role to expand significantly.

Hack.bio: A Fishman Karate master in the Revolutionary Army. Known for his exceptional combat ability and loyalty to the cause. Participated in the Dressrosa Corrida Colosseum as part of the Army's mission.
Hack.events: His Reverie involvement and confirmed active status in the Revolutionary Army keeps stock stable. As the Army's final saga role grows, Hack benefits from collective faction momentum.

Kyros.bio: Dressrosa's greatest gladiator with 3,000+ victories undefeated — a legend who was turned into a toy soldier for a decade but never stopped fighting to protect his daughter Rebecca. His resilience is the human heart of Dressrosa.
Kyros.events: The Dressrosa arc conclusion — Kyros's transformation back and reunion with Rebecca — was an emotional peak that drove community stock to a high. His legendary gladiator status keeps his floor firm.

Rebecca.bio: Princess of Dressrosa and daughter of the legendary Kyros. A gladiator who fought in the Corrida Colosseum under the rule of never wounding an opponent — a testament to her gentle nature in a brutal world.
Rebecca.events: Her Dressrosa arc resolution — reuniting with her father — was a beloved community moment. Stock holds steady on fond memories and her restored royal life.

Viola.bio: Princess of Dressrosa who once operated as CP0 agent 'Violet' under Doflamingo's control. Her Giro Giro no Mi allows her to see through anything and read minds — an invaluable intelligence asset.
Viola.events: Her defection from Doflamingo and aid to Sanji and the Straw Hats was a turning point in Dressrosa. Community respects her sacrifice and princess role, keeping stock steady with mild upward bias.

Vegapunk Shaka.bio: Vegapunk Satellite #01 representing 'Good.' The most calm and analytical of the satellites, Shaka guided the Straw Hats through Egghead Island and made critical decisions to protect Vegapunk's legacy.
Vegapunk Shaka.events: Shaka's death — shot by York — was one of Egghead's most shocking moments. His stock peaked on his leadership role then declined on death. Community preserves him as a legacy figure.

Vegapunk Edison.bio: Vegapunk Satellite #02 representing 'Exorcism' — the inventor satellite who generated ideas at lightning speed. His mechanical body and rapid innovation made him a key part of Vegapunk's scientific network.
Vegapunk Edison.events: Killed at Egghead as part of York's betrayal. Stock followed the Egghead peak-then-decline pattern of the deceased satellites. His inventive legacy keeps him from fading completely.

Vegapunk Pythagoras.bio: Vegapunk Satellite #03 representing 'Wisdom.' A mechanical satellite body built for pure computation and data processing — the most artificially constructed of the six.
Vegapunk Pythagoras.events: Destroyed at Egghead. Stock rose with the full Satellite ensemble reveal then fell sharply post-death. Community values him as part of the Egghead ensemble rather than individually.

Vegapunk Atlas.bio: Vegapunk Satellite #04 representing 'Violence.' Despite the intimidating title, Atlas's physical satellite body charged headfirst into combat. She survived Egghead and journeyed with the Straw Hats toward Elbaf.
Vegapunk Atlas.events: Her survival of Egghead and continued presence aboard the crew's journey keeps her stock rising post-arc. As the only surviving combat-capable satellite, community interest in her Elbaf role is growing.

Vegapunk York.bio: Vegapunk Satellite #05 representing 'Greed.' The traitor who sold out Egghead Island to the World Government in exchange for becoming a Celestial Dragon. Her betrayal triggered the entire Egghead siege.
Vegapunk York.events: York's betrayal was the pivot point of the entire Egghead arc — sending community stock on a massive spike on reveal. Her successful achievement of Celestial Dragon status keeps her volatile and high-value into the final saga.

Vegapunk Lilith.bio: Vegapunk Satellite #06 representing 'Evil.' Despite the name, Lilith showed considerable courage and creativity during the Egghead siege. Her battle suit and weaponized approach made her one of the more striking satellites.
Vegapunk Lilith.events: Her survival post-Egghead and the general community appreciation for her visual design and personality keep her stock steady. Expected to appear in the final saga alongside Atlas.

Hannyabal.bio: Chief Warden of Impel Down following Magellan's demotion — a man who openly admitted he wanted to become Fleet Admiral but whose genuine justice and courage under fire earned real respect.
Hannyabal.events: His comically honest ambition and surprisingly brave performance during the Marineford war kept his stock higher than expected. Stable post-Marineford with a modest community appreciation premium.

Wapol.bio: Former King of Drum Island who fled his people during a Warlord invasion, was dethroned by Luffy, and somehow clawed his way to becoming a weapons magnate — and eventually a Celestial Dragon.
Wapol.events: Wapol's improbable rise from comic villain to Celestial Dragon is one of the story's darkest jokes. His surprise Reverie appearance and subsequent elevation spiked stock. His Egghead-era testimony against Vegapunk keeps him relevant.

Ichiji.events: His Whole Cake Island role saving Sanji's crew pushed stock upward. The Germa 66 story arc closed with community appreciation for the sibling bond. Stock holds steady at respected mid-tier commander level.
