Niji.events: Despite his abrasive personality, Niji's Whole Cake Island intervention earned reluctant community respect. Stock stabilized at a solid tier reflecting his genuine combat capability.

Yonji.bio: Youngest of the Vinsmoke brothers and Winch Green of Germa 66. His mechanical suit enhances his already formidable physicality, and his winch-based attacks give him unique range in combat.
Yonji.events: The least prominent Vinsmoke brother, Yonji's stock trails his siblings slightly. His WCI participation and Germa's collective role keep his valuation steady with the rest of the unit.

Whitey Bay.bio: Division Commander of the Whitebeard Pirates and the 'Ice Witch' — her icebreaker ship and cold-weather fighting style made her one of the most recognizable female commanders in the New World.
Whitey Bay.events: Her Marineford performance was solid but brief. Stock reflects a respected commander tier without individual spotlight moments. Expected to appear in Marco's Whitebeard legacy storyline.

Aladdin.bio: Doctor of the Sun Pirates and a close ally of Boa Hancock. He helped Fisher Tiger's crew maintain its humanitarian mission and provides medical support to Amazon Lily's forces.
Aladdin.events: Stock grew with Fisher Tiger's backstory reveal and his continued presence supporting Hancock. His role in protecting Amazon Lily during the Blackbeard conflict pushed values slightly upward.

Clover.bio: Lead scholar of Ohara who dedicated his life to understanding the Void Century. He was moments from revealing the truth to the world when the Buster Call silenced him — the most courageous act in the series' history.
Clover.events: Every Void Century revelation adds to Clover's posthumous stock. The Egghead flashback showing his research was preserved by Vegapunk pushed his legacy value to new highs. He died telling the truth.

Don Krieg.bio: Self-proclaimed Great Pirate of the East Blue and commander of a 50-ship armada. Krieg relied on an enormous arsenal of hidden weapons — a villain who weaponized cowardice into a fighting style.
Don Krieg.events: A purely historical figure in current story terms. His defeat by Luffy and Sanji's combined effort at the Baratie is iconic but ancient — stock holds at East Blue nostalgia level with no growth potential.

Sora.bio: Mother of the Vinsmoke siblings who secretly took a drug during pregnancy to preserve her children's humanity despite Judge's genetic modifications. She died from the side effects — giving her children the ability to feel.
Sora.events: Sora's sacrifice is the emotional backbone of the entire Vinsmoke story. Her stock is a pure legacy value — frozen at her WCI revelation and held as an eternal tribute by the community.

Absalom.bio: Former commander of Thriller Bark with the Clear-Clear Fruit (Suke Suke no Mi) granting invisibility. His fruit was stolen by Blackbeard after his death — making him one of the first confirmed fruit inheritance victims.
Absalom.events: His death at Blackbeard's hands and the revelation that his fruit was stolen were shocking Wano-era revelations. Stock peaked at that moment — now a memorial figure with no growth potential.

Caribou.bio: Captain of the Caribou Pirates with the Swamp-Swamp Logia Fruit. A chaotic opportunist who gleaned knowledge of the Ancient Weapons from Shirahoshi and spied for a mysterious third party during Wano.
Caribou.events: His unknown employer's identity and his specific knowledge of Ancient Weapon locations drives enormous speculation. Elbaf-era community stock is rising steadily as his espionage role seems set to pay off in the final saga.

Emet.bio: The Iron Giant — an ancient robot from the Void Century that reactivated on Egghead Island. Its awakening began when Luffy achieved Gear Fifth, directly tied to Joy Boy's return. One of the most lore-significant reveals of the entire series.
Emet.events: First appeared dormant on Egghead. Reactivated and began moving on its own, shocking the entire fandom. The Joy Boy chest reveal sent community hype to stratospheric levels — this is an Ancient Weapon-tier entity with enormous unresolved narrative weight.

Gin.bio: First mate of Don Krieg and one of Sanji's most memorable early opponents. A fearsome fighter known as Man-Demon Gin, who showed genuine humanity when he protected Sanji despite being gassed with MH5. Disappeared after East Blue — for 25 years of publication time.
Gin.events: Gin's return at Elbaf in chapter 1117 after a 25-year absence caused an explosion of community nostalgia and hype. His sudden reappearance from the very beginning of the story signals Oda has plans for him — stock spiked dramatically.

Pandaman.bio: The ultimate background character — a panda-headed figure that has appeared in over 100 chapters hidden in crowds, panels, and scenes across the entire series. Oda's personal Easter egg. He has an official bounty poster and is treated as genuine One Piece lore.
Pandaman.events: Fan communities have catalogued every single Pandaman appearance across 25+ years of manga. When his official bounty poster was revealed, the internet erupted. He represents the meta-awareness and love between Oda and his community — pure cultural stock.

Batchee.bio: A fly. A literal, named fly. Batchee appeared as background scenery and was officially named in an SBS column. He ranked 112th in an official One Piece character popularity poll — above many named human characters.
Batchee.events: The fact that a fly received an official name, an SBS mention, and polled above actual characters is the purest distillation of One Piece's absurdist humor. Batchee is a community in-joke with legitimate official backing.

Gaimon.bio: A pirate who fell into an empty treasure chest and became permanently stuck. He spent 20 years alone on an island guarding treasure boxes — which turned out to all be empty. Eventually found companionship with unique hybrid animals and chose to stay.
Gaimon.events: Gaimon is one of the most beloved East Blue characters for his emotional story and absurd design. His cover story showing his happy life with his animal friends cemented his legacy. He represents the heartfelt melancholy Oda hides in early arcs.

Hanafuda.bio: A mysterious former Warlord of the Sea revealed in SBS to be the father of Ulti and Page One. Nothing is known about his power or current status — but any parent of two Ancient Zoan users must be extraordinary.
Hanafuda.events: The SBS revelation of his existence caused immediate community speculation. A secret Warlord who fathered two of Kaido's Tobiroppo is an irresistible mystery. Community stock reflects the enormous unanswered questions surrounding his identity and role.

Davy Jones.bio: The legendary ghost of the deep — Oda confirmed in SBS that the 'Davy Back Fight' takes its name from the real-world nautical myth of Davy Jones' Locker: the abyss at the bottom of the ocean where drowned pirates' souls sink forever. Oda drew this figure in an SBS illustration. He is not a confirmed canon character, but Oda's deliberate naming and illustration give him official mythological standing in the One Piece world.
Davy Jones.events: Davy Jones entered the site as a community theory character born from Oda's own SBS explanation of the Davy Back Fight's pirate mythology origins. His SBS illustration is the closest thing to canon he has. Each Void Century revelation and deep-sea lore drop sends his community stock climbing. He is myth made stock — and myths never fully die.

sbs.text: Oda explained the 'Davy Back Fight' name in SBS: it references the real-world nautical legend of Davy Jones' Locker — the mythical abyss at the ocean floor where the souls of drowned pirates sink for eternity. Oda drew an illustration of this figure. This SBS column is the only official One Piece acknowledgement of Davy Jones. He is pirate mythology that Oda made canon-adjacent by drawing him himself.

The Davy Back Fight game itself — where pirates stake crewmates against each other — is named after this legend. In the myth, Davy Jones claims sailors for his locker. In the game, pirates claim each other. Oda translated the myth into a game mechanic directly.

Chinjao.bio: One of the legendary pirates of the previous era — a man whose drill-like head could shatter frozen continents and whose bounty once exceeded 500,000,000 beri. Commander of the Happou Navy and grandfather of Sai. Garp destroyed his special head (and access to his buried treasure) with a single punch decades before the story began.
Chinjao.events: His Dressrosa tournament appearance against Luffy was the old era colliding with the new — a living legend who had once terrorized the seas, instantly outclassed. His defeat dropped stock, but the historical prestige and Sai's ongoing Grand Fleet arc keep a meaningful floor. Stock declines slowly as his era fades further.

sbs.text: Oda confirmed in SBS that Garp's legendary headbutt flattened Chinjao's drill-tip during their fight — costing Chinjao the ability to pierce the frozen ocean floor where his treasure was buried. The defeat wasn't just physical humiliation: it locked away his fortune for decades. Chinjao's entire Dressrosa arc is about reclaiming what that punch took from him.

Pedro.bio: The Ruler of the Guardians of Zou and former captain of the Nox Pirates — a Jaguar Mink who spent years sailing for the Poneglyphs, believing the dawn of the world was worth dying for. He said he gave his lifespan to Crocus years earlier, and spent what remained ensuring the Straw Hats could escape Whole Cake Island.
Pedro.events: His explosion against Baron Tamago at WCI — deliberately detonating himself to buy the crew their escape window — is one of the most emotionally resonant deaths in the series. Stock parked above his canon bounty on community love. The Pedro of the Treetops memorial premium is real and durable.

Pekoms.bio: A Lion Mink serving as an officer of the Big Mom Pirates — one of the few Minks in her crew, capable of Sulong transformation under a full moon. He ate the Kame Kame no Mi, giving him a turtle shell impervious enough to tank Big Mom's strikes. His loyalty was perpetually split between duty to Linlin and gratitude to the Straw Hats who protect Fishman Island.
Pekoms.events: After being shot by Capone Bege and left in the ocean near Cacao Island, Pekoms has not appeared since. His fate is unresolved. Stock holds on Sulong capability and Mink heritage, suppressed by the complete absence of post-WCI appearances.

Carrot.bio: A Rabbit Mink from Zou and member of the Inuarashi Musketeer Squad who stowed away on the Straw Hats' ship to Whole Cake Island. Her Sulong transformation under the full moon of WCI turned a surprise companion into a tier-breaking wildcard. She was named the new ruler of the Mink Tribe by Nekomamushi and Inuarashi after Wano — remaining behind to lead Zou into the final saga.
Carrot.events: Her Sulong debut at WCI was a genuine community shock — no one predicted a stowaway rabbit would produce one of the arc's standout power moments. Her departure from the crew was bittersweet. As ruler of an allied kingdom with Sulong capability, the community expects her return. Stock trends upward on unresolved potential.

Avalo Pizarro.bio: One of Blackbeard's Ten Titanic Captains, formerly a tyrannical king known for his cruelty. He wields the Shima Shima no Mi — the Island-Island Fruit — which allows him to merge with and take control of entire islands, becoming a continental-scale weapon. There is theoretically no upper size limit to what he can absorb.
Avalo Pizarro.events: As one of Blackbeard's senior commanders with a Devil Fruit that has no obvious ceiling, Pizarro's stock climbs steadily as the Yonko Blackbeard moves toward the final confrontation. Community speculation on his true power scale keeps his chart trending up through every arc.

Morgans.bio: President of the World Economy News Paper — the most powerful information broker in the world. His control over what gets published and suppressed gives him political leverage comparable to a Yonko. He covered the Reverie's aftermath, broadcast Wano's revolution to the globe, and has repeatedly defied World Government censorship with gleeful drama.
Morgans.events: Morgans' decision to publish the full truth of the Reverie — overriding World Government blackout orders — was one of the biggest narrative pivots of the final saga setup. His ongoing role as the world's information gatekeeper makes him a non-combat stock that grows with every arc he influences.

Baron Tamago.bio: An officer of the Big Mom Pirates and one of her most distinctive soldiers. He ate the Tama Tama no Mi — an Egg Paramecia that transforms each defeat into rebirth: Baron Tamago cracks into Viscount Hiyoko, then hatches further into Count Niwatori. He is never truly down until the third form falls.
Baron Tamago.events: His two-round fight with Pedro at WCI — forced into all three egg forms before Pedro sacrificed himself — was the standout moment of his career. Stock has not moved significantly post-WCI but holds on the unique revival mechanic and officer-level combat record.

Inazuma.bio: A Revolutionary Army officer and one of Emporio Ivankov's closest allies. He ate the Choki Choki no Mi — the Clip-Clip Fruit — allowing him to cut any material as if it were paper and rearrange the pieces. During the Marineford War he used this ability to literally reshape the execution platform, buying Luffy crucial seconds.
Inazuma.events: His Marineford performance was decisive and underrated — battlefield manipulation on a scale few Paramecia users can match. Stock has plateaued in the Revolutionary Army's quiet phase, but the Army's inevitable final saga role keeps the ceiling open. The Clip-Clip Fruit's creative ceiling is perpetually underpriced by the community.

Flampe.bio: The 100th daughter of Charlotte Linlin and one of Katakuri's most devoted fans. She attempted to influence the Luffy vs Katakuri battle by shooting micro-darts that numbed Luffy mid-fight — and watched her idol immediately self-scar his own face to match what she caused, making her interference meaningless and humiliating.
Flampe.events: Her arc is a brief community joke. The irony of being punished by her own idol for trying to help him is perfectly executed. Stock parked below canon bounty — humiliation tax applied. No appearances since WCI.

Vander Decken IX.bio: The ninth successor of the Vander Decken name, wielder of the Mato Mato no Mi — a Devil Fruit that permanently marks any target he touches, ensuring every thrown object seeks them forever. He used this ability to pursue a delusional courtship of Shirahoshi, hurling increasingly large projectiles at the mermaid princess he had been stalking since she was six years old.
Vander Decken IX.events: A villain whose premise is so inherently disturbing that community stock carries a permanent reputational discount. Defeated first by Hody Jones then finished by Luffy. His Devil Fruit has genuine theoretical depth — but in Decken's hands it became a delivery mechanism for a creepy stalker arc. Stock at near-zero post-defeat.

Hyouzou.bio: The strongest swordsman in Fishman Island — a blue-ringed octopus Fishman who wielded eight swords simultaneously across eight arms. A mercenary who fought for whoever paid rather than any ideology, Hyouzou was the New Fishman Pirates' most dangerous hire. His fight with Roronoa Zoro lasted approximately one chapter.
Hyouzou.events: The setup was excellent — eight swords, monstrous strength, a feared freelance killer. The payoff was Zoro winning drunk, with one sword, without trying. That result defines community perception. Stock reflects the gap between the hype of introduction and the reality of delivery.

Ikaros Much.bio: An officer of the New Fishman Pirates — a pike squid Fishman known for his 'Hell Wrist' attacks. One of Hody Jones' five commanders, tasked with enforcing NFP authority across Fishman Island.
Ikaros Much.events: Defeated during the Fishman Island arc alongside the rest of the NFP leadership. No appearances since. Stock parked at defeat floor — a placeholder villain who served the arc's structure rather than its story.

Zeo.bio: An officer of the New Fishman Pirates — a wobbegong shark Fishman with near-perfect natural camouflage. Zeo's preferred tactic was psychological: he would retreat invisibly mid-battle and blame his own allies for the ground he lost, claiming he was never hit.
Zeo.events: His cowardly battlefield psychology made him memorable for comedy rather than combat. Defeated at Fishman Island. Stock at defeat floor — the camouflage gimmick had more potential than his actual arc delivered.

Dosun.bio: An officer of the New Fishman Pirates — a hammerhead shark Fishman whose power fluctuates with his emotional state. When fired up he is formidable; when dejected he is a pushover. His rapid mood swings between aggressive ranting and complete defeat were one of Fishman Island's running gags.
Dosun.events: A gimmick character whose mood mechanics were genuinely creative but underused. Defeated at Fishman Island by the post-timeskip Straw Hats. Stock at defeat floor.

Daruma.bio: An officer of the New Fishman Pirates — a cookie-cutter shark Fishman small in stature but violent in execution. His teeth could bite through solid stone, and his aggressive fighting style made him the most reckless of the five commanders.
Daruma.events: Defeated at Fishman Island, serving primarily as a demonstration of the Straw Hats' post-timeskip capabilities. Stock at defeat floor — no appearances or story relevance since.

Wadatsumi.bio: A giant pufferfish Fishman who began the story as part of Hody Jones' muscle — capable of inflating himself to monstrous size for overwhelming physical attacks. After the Fishman Island arc he reformed and joined the Sun Pirates, finding purpose in the crew originally built by Fisher Tiger.
Wadatsumi.events: His quiet arc from villain to Sun Pirate ally is one of Fishman Island's understated feel-good moments. Stock holds slightly above his canon bounty on ongoing alliance value. As Jinbe's former crewmates, the Sun Pirates may yet find a role in the final saga.

Elizabello II.bio: King of the Prodence Kingdom and the wielder of the King Punch — a single strike so destructive it reportedly requires one full hour of preparation and can annihilate an entire pirate crew on delivery. He entered the Dressrosa tournament seeking the Flame-Flame Fruit for his nation.
Elizabello II.events: The King Punch became an instant community meme — the ultimate one-hit attack requiring sixty minutes of windup, immediately parried by Bellamy mid-arc. His Reverie appearance elevated the political dimension. Stock is sustained almost entirely by meme energy and the theoretical ceiling of a one-hour-charge strike that has never landed cleanly.

Suleiman.bio: A former military commander who turned pirate after a controversial career, earning the nickname 'the Beheader.' He competed in the Dressrosa Corrida Colosseum, and after Doflamingo's defeat pledged fealty to Cavendish as part of the Straw Hat Grand Fleet.
Suleiman.events: His Grand Fleet membership elevates stock above his raw bounty. Military discipline and genuine combat experience make him one of the more credible small-tier Grand Fleet members. Stock grows slowly alongside the fleet's increasing final saga relevance.

Leo.bio: Captain of the Tontatta Pirates of Green Bit and commander of one of the Straw Hat Grand Fleet's member crews. He ate the Nui Nui no Mi — the Stitch-Stitch Fruit — allowing him to stitch any objects or living beings together or apart. Leo was instrumental in liberating the Tontatta from centuries of slavery under Doflamingo's operation.
Leo.events: His role in freeing the Tontatta people — coordinating underground resistance during Dressrosa — earned real community respect. Grand Fleet membership and captaincy of his own crew give him ongoing story stakes. Stock grows steadily as the fleet's final saga arc approaches.

Oars Jr..bio: A massive ancient giant descended from the legendary demon Oars — one of the titans referenced in Elbaf mythology alongside names like Loki and Harald. He fought at Marineford for Whitebeard out of devotion to Portgas D. Ace, withstanding attacks from multiple Warlords including having his leg severed by Doflamingo, and still pushed forward.
Oars Jr..events: His survival of Marineford despite catastrophic wounds established him as a figure of sheer resilience. With the Elbaf arc placing ancient giant mythology — the Oars bloodline, the Warrior of Liberation, the mythic giants — at the story's center, community speculation about his role has surged. Any bearer of the Oars bloodline carries significant lore premium in the current arc.

Pound.bio: The 25th husband of Charlotte Linlin — one of many men she took, used, and discarded. He is the biological father of Lola and Chiffon, and spent years searching for his daughters after being cast aside by Big Mom. He found Chiffon briefly during the Whole Cake Island arc, confirmed she was alive and happy, and was killed by Charlotte Oven shortly after.
Pound.events: A one-arc minor character whose death landed harder than his screentime deserved. He died smiling, having seen his daughter one last time. Stock holds a small memorial premium above zero purely on the emotional weight of that moment — a quiet gut-punch in a loud arc.

Jaguar D. Saul.bio: Jaguar D. Saul is a former Marine Vice Admiral who refused to participate in the Buster Call on Ohara. Defying direct orders, he helped Nico Robin escape — and was encased in ice by his former colleague Kuzan as punishment. Believed dead for twenty-two years, he survived when the Buster Call's own flames eventually melted Kuzan's ice, allowing him to fall into the ocean. He made his way to Elbaf, where he spent over two decades as a history teacher at the Warrior's Spring, quietly gathering and preserving every book the Giants had rescued from Ohara's destruction. He was reunited with Robin in chapter 1133, revealing the Owl Library — the most complete surviving record of Ohara's research.
Jaguar D. Saul.events: Jaguar D. Saul's Elbaf reveal answered what the community had been sitting on since Enies Lobby. He survived because the Buster Call's flames melted Kuzan's ice before it fully claimed him, letting him fall into the ocean. For twenty-two years he lived in Elbaf as a history teacher, building the Owl Library — preserving every book the Giants rescued from Ohara's destruction, gigantified by Biblo's Iku Iku no Mi. The Buster Call erased Ohara but not its knowledge. The Holy Knights' attack on the library — taking children hostage, forcing the Giants to burn their own school — was the World Government's second attempt to achieve what the first failed to accomplish. Saul's market position is inseparable from Robin's: the archivist and the archaeologist represent the same thesis, and both charts move together. He is the Owl Library's custodian, and the Owl Library is the final saga's most important surviving asset outside the Poneglyphs themselves.
